in_text_mentions: Extensor tendon disruption of the fingers in zone 1 according to Verdan occurs as a closed injury in 75% of the cases and is the most common tendon injury of the hand [4–6]. A bony mallet finger is the result of an avulsion of the extensor tendon from the distal finger phalanx with a small or large fragment of bone attached to the avulsed tendon (Fig. 1) and needs special attention and treatment.Fig. 1X-ray of a bony mallet finger: a posterior–anterior and b lateral

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of a hand showing the index finger with a flexed distal phalanx, consistent with mallet finger deformity. The article title is 'Mallet Finger Lattice Casts Using 3D Printing,' and the in-text mentions scanning the index finger while maintaining posture of the extensor tendon. Although the caption does not explicitly describe the deformity, the visual appearance supports the diagnosis.

in_text_mentions: First, the index finger was scanned repeatedly while maintaining posture of the extensor tendon (Figure 2) using a 3D scanner (3D Systems Sense scanner) to generate a stereolithography (STL) file of the finger. STL files, the end result of the 3D modelling process, are typically generated by computer-aided design (CAD) programs, which use this file type to store information about 3D models. The STL file shows the surface shape of a 3D object without representation of colour, texture, or other general characteristics of the model.
